question: What was the original name of Jim Corbett National Park when it was established in 1936 as the first national park in Asia?
explanation: Corbett National Park, spread across parts of Nainital and Pauri Garhwal districts, is described as India’s and Asia’s first national park. It was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, named after Sir Malcolm Hailey, then Governor of the United Provinces. After independence, it was renamed Ramganga National Park in 1954 and Corbett National Park in 1957 in memory of naturalist and hunter Jim Corbett. India’s Project Tiger was launched here on 1 April 1973, according to the source.

question: Which wetland in Uttarakhand became the state’s first Ramsar Site, recognised as a wetland of international importance in October 2020?
explanation: Asan Conservation Reserve lies near Dakpathar in Dehradun district, at the confluence of the Yamuna and Asan rivers. The source gives its area as 444.4 hectares and says it was recognised on 15 October 2020 as Uttarakhand’s first Ramsar Site (Ramsar Site No. 2437). The wetland provides important winter habitat for migratory waterbirds, including ruddy shelduck, pochards and mallards, along the Central Asian Flyway. question: In which Uttarakhand city is the CSIR–Central Building Research Institute (CBRI), dedicated to research on earthquake-resistant buildings, disaster-resilient structures and indigenous construction materials, located?
explanation: The Central Building Research Institute (CSIR-CBRI) is a major national laboratory of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research located in Roorkee, Haridwar district, Uttarakhand. Established in 1947, it conducts research on earthquake-resistant structures, affordable disaster-resilient housing, energy-efficient buildings and fire-resistant construction materials. The source also says that CBRI Roorkee designed the scientific mechanism for the ‘Surya Tilak’ effect at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.

question: Which environmental activist, widely known as the ‘Chipko Woman’, led 27 women in Reni village, Chamoli district, on 26 March 1974 to embrace trees and stop contractors from felling them?
explanation: On 26 March 1974, when many men from Reni village near Joshimath were away in Chamoli, logging contractors arrived to cut trees. unit: Unit 5: Indian Forests—Forest Survey of India
question: Where is the national headquarters of the Forest Survey of India (FSI), which publishes the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) and assesses forest and tree cover every two years?
explanation: The Forest Survey of India is a national organisation under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, with its headquarters on Kaulagarh Road in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It was established on 1 June 1981 through the reorganisation of the Pre-Investment Survey of Forest Resources. Using satellite data and other methods, it assesses the country’s forest and tree cover and publishes the India State of Forest Report at two-year intervals.

question: In November 2025, the 30th UN Climate Change Conference (COP30) was held in which city, described as a gateway to the Amazon rainforest?
